newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to open office for five allies.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to open office for five allies.

text.p: Taiwan will open a joint office for five Central American allies this month to consolidate ties with them in the face of a diplomatic tug-of-war with rival China, a top official said on Tuesday.
"We expect the Central American Economic and Trade Office will be opened at the end of June," Huang Hsing-kuo, the office chief, told Reuters.
The establishment of the office for Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Nicaragua would help thwart China's attempts to woo the allies of Taiwan, officials said.
China, which views Taiwan as a rebel-held province since they split at the end of a civil war in 1949, has warned other countries against forging ties with the island.

Huang said the five countries wanted more Taiwanese trade and investment. Taiwan's two-way trade with the five Central American nations amounted to US$260.1 million in 1996, with Taiwan exporting US$235.3 million to those countries.

"Because of inadequate promotion, Taiwan businessmen are not highly interested in trading with or investing in Central America," Huang said, adding the office's main work was to help change this situation.
He said its major work would include helping those countries increase sales in Taiwan, and encouraging Taiwan people to invest in and visit the region.

Huang, formerly secretary-general of Taiwan's quasi-official China External Trade Development Council, said the office was originally scheduled to be opened on Monday, but the opening was postponed to fit in with a planned state visit by Costa Rican president Jose Maria Figueres.
He said the operational funds of the office would come from the interest earnings from Taiwan's deposits at the Central American Bank of Economic Cooperation and Integration.
